title: Staged precision degradation with speculative kernel prober and rollback window
author: Maya Patel
description: Introduce a staged precision degradation mechanism that probes lower-precision kernels (INT8/FP16) speculatively while keeping a correctness rollback window to ensure no silent regressions. This PR implements a speculative kernel prober that runs a lightweight probe alongside the production high-precision path for a configurable fraction of requests, a rollback handshake that compares summary metrics/digests rather than full outputs to avoid token-level cost, and a non-blocking fallback handshake for continuous batching and KV cache coherence. Motivation: customers have asked for lower per-token cost but we must avoid silent quality regressions or KV cache inconsistencies when toggling precision at runtime. The change aims to make the fast/int8 path safe-by-default while preserving latency SLOs and cache correctness across batch boundaries. Key behaviors: 1) Speculative prober runs in parallel only for requests matching the probe filter (traffic percentage + bucketed prompt shapes). 2) Probe produces a short statistical digest (token n-gram hashes + top-k distribution sketch) that is compared against the high-precision digest inside a micro-rollback window (first N tokens or until a configured stability metric). 3) If the digest divergence exceeds the threshold, we mark the kernel as "candidate-untrusted" and route similar shaped requests to safe-mode for a cooldown period. 4) For continuous batching, we avoid blocking the batch while waiting for probe comparison by attaching a deferred reconciliation step that can still trigger a model-level rollback and evict/repair KV cache entries if divergence is detected post-facto. 5) Added observability hooks and a rollout safe-guard so operators can ramp probe fraction and thresholds. This PR is focused on runtime orchestration and correctness plumbing; kernel implementations for specific backends are mocked behind the KernelProbe interface and exercised via integration tests. Checklist: [x] kernel prober control plane and config knobs [x] digest generation and comparator [x] non-blocking rollback/reconciliation flow [x] metrics + tracing for probe outcomes [x] integration tests for batching + KV coherence [x] docs update and rollout guide in runtime/ops/PROBING.md

review_comments: Liam Chen: Overall this looks promising. My main concern is the cost of running probes in parallel for long contexts — can we bound memory/dedicated device usage?

Author (Maya): We cap speculative probes to a small in-process worker pool by default and the prober emits an early-abort if sequence length or token cost exceeds thresholds. Config knobs exposed so ops can set device affinity if desired.
Sophie Ramos: The digest comparator needs to avoid being gamed by small reorderings in top-k. Suggest switching to an earth-mover style metric or KL with smoothing.
Author (Maya): Switched comparator to a smoothed KL with heavy tail clamping; added a tunable divergence threshold and unit tests demonstrating stability.
Vikram Singh: How do we guarantee KV cache coherence if reconciliation runs after batches commit? Potential stale pointer issues.

Author (Maya): We implemented a conservative repair path: reconciliation can mark keys as 'repaired' and schedule eviction+refetch for affected request IDs; we also added an opt-in strict-mode which blocks commit until probe comparison completes for high-SLA buckets.
Liam Chen: CI integration failed on first run due to a timing race in the mock prober. Please re-run with the fix.
Author (Maya): Fixed race and added deterministic seeding for the mock kernels; re-ran CI and confirmed green.
Sophie Ramos: Approve after a small nit on comments in batcher.go.
Vikram Singh: Approve, would like telemetry dashboard follow-up (ticket linked).
release_notes: Adds staged precision probing infrastructure: speculative kernel prober, digest comparator, non-blocking rollback and KV cache reconciliation. Operators should review runtime/config/probing.yaml before ramping probe fractions. See runtime/ops/PROBING.md for rollout guidance.
